jobs.title: Advanced Practice Provider (APP/NP/PA) Pediatric Cardiology Acute Care
jobs.summary: Advanced Practice Provider (APP/NP/PA) Pediatric Cardiology Acute Care at UVA Health Children's. Setting: pediatric inpatient specialty service. Notable: new grad friendly, nights, CPNP-AC required.
jobs.description:
Join UVA Children's growing Pediatric Cardiology team as we prepare for an exciting expansion of our cardiac inpatient services in the new South Tower. We are seeking Advanced Practice Providers (NPs/PAs) to provide comprehensive care for pediatric cardiac patients admitted to the General Cardiology and Heart Failure/Transplant services. APPs will work collaboratively with Pediatric Cardiology attending physicians, fellows, and an interdisciplinary team to provide high-quality, family-centered care for children with complex cardiac conditions.

This position supports the dedicated Cardiology Acute Care service, providing care for patients who do not require CICU or CIMU level care. Critical Care APPs will provide separate coverage for patients in the CICU/CIMU. The new cardiac program is anticipated to open on 7 South in spring 2028, with opportunities to join the team in advance for comprehensive orientation and specialty training.

Schedule and Position Details:

FTE: 1.0

Schedule: Three 12-hour shifts per week, plus one additional 12-hour shift every four weeks.

Shifts: Rotating days, nights, weekends, and holidays.

Shift Differential: Available for eligible shifts.

Coverage: 24/7 inpatient service with two daytime APPs and one in-house overnight APP.

Location: UVA Children's, with planned transition to 7 South in the South Tower.

Team Structure: Collaborative, attending-led Pediatric Cardiology service with APP and fellow support.

Onboarding: Comprehensive orientation and specialty training, tailored to experience, with up to 6–12 months of onboarding and competency development.

This is an opportunity to help build and shape an expanding pediatric cardiac inpatient program while developing specialized expertise in the care of children with congenital and acquired heart disease, heart failure, and cardiac transplantation.

Preferred Qualifications:

National certification appropriate to professional licensure. Nurse Practitioner candidates must be Acute Care certified (CPNP-AC).

Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) certification or ability to obtain prior to clinical practice.

Strong interest in pediatric cardiology and caring for children with complex cardiac conditions.

Commitment to working rotating day, night, weekend, and holiday shifts.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Acute care certification preferred.

Previous clinical experience in inpatient pediatric cardiology, pediatric critical care, or pediatric acute care.

Experience caring for children with congenital or acquired heart disease, heart failure, or cardiac transplantation.

Strong clinical assessment, critical thinking, communication, and interdisciplinary collaboration skills.

Current DEA registration and prescriptive authority, as applicable to professional licensure.

New graduates are encouraged to apply. Comprehensive orientation, specialty-specific training, and a structured onboarding program are provided to support successful transition into the pediatric cardiology inpatient role.

1) Administration

Member of the Division of Pediatric Cardiology, Department of Pediatrics.

Part of the APP expansion supporting the dedicated Cardiology Acute Care service, increasing staffing from 1.0 to 7.5 APP FTE.

Position funded 90% by the Medical Center and 10% by the Department of Pediatrics.

Assigned to the General Pediatric Cardiology or Heart Failure/Transplant service based on clinical and operational needs.

Based in the South Tower, 7 South, at the anticipated spring 2028 opening, with acute-care services transitioning to 7 West or 7 Central as the program expands.

Full-time schedule consisting of three 12-hour shifts per week and one additional 12-hour shift every four weeks, including rotating days, nights, weekends, and holidays. Eligible shifts receive shift differential compensation.

2) Professional

Complete comprehensive orientation and specialty-specific competency development, which may require 6–12 months depending on experience.

Practice within the division's inpatient coverage model, supporting compliance with ACGME requirements.

Collaborate with Pediatric Cardiology attending physicians, cardiology fellows, and interdisciplinary team members to provide high-quality, evidence-based, family-centered care.

Maintain clinical competencies and participate in ongoing professional development specific to pediatric cardiology, congenital heart disease, and heart failure/transplant care.

3) Clinical

Provide direct clinical management of pediatric cardiac acute-care patients under the leadership of Pediatric Cardiology attending physicians.

Perform daily assessments, develop and implement treatment plans, review diagnostic studies, manage admissions and discharges, and coordinate care for assigned patients.

Provide consistent day, overnight, weekend, and holiday coverage for the dedicated Cardiology Acute Care service.

Support continuity of care for patients transitioning between critical-care and acute-care settings, collaborating with the Critical Care APPs and physicians responsible for CICU/CIMU patients.

Collaborate with echocardiography, cardiac catheterization, electrophysiology, fetal cardiology, heart failure, and transplant teams to coordinate comprehensive patient care.

Recognize changes in patient condition, initiate appropriate interventions, and facilitate escalation to critical care when indicated.

4) Leadership

Participate in the development and implementation of the dedicated Pediatric Cardiology Acute Care service as the cardiac program expands into the South Tower.

Contribute to the development and refinement of clinical workflows, care coordination processes, and evidence-based practices supporting safe and efficient inpatient care.

Support ongoing evaluation of staffing and clinical needs as patient volume, acuity, and the cardiac acute-care footprint expand.

jobs.title: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) Advanced Practice Provider
jobs.summary: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) Advanced Practice Provider at Maine Medical Center. Setting: NICU / neonatology. Notable: new grad friendly, nights, relocation assistance.
jobs.description:
Maine Medical Center Barbara Bush Children’s Hospital in Portland, Maine - Maine’s only full-service Level IV NICU children’s hospital, is recruiting for an experienced full-time (1.00 FTE/40 hrs) Advanced Practice Provider (APP); a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner, Acute Care Certified Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, or a Physician Associate/Assistant. This is a combined day and night position and new grads with a strong neonatal background are encouraged to apply.

The APP will provide detailed and comprehensive assessment and treatment of neonatal patients within the framework of safe patient and family centered care. The APP will be responsible for attending high-risk deliveries, as well as functioning as the lead on neonatal transports. The scope of practice encompasses the development and recording of a plan for care in collaboration with family, multidisciplinary team members, and community resources for both chronic and episodic illnesses.

Desired Qualifications & Experience:

·Excellence in interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively with all MHMMC departments, families, and members of the multidisciplinary health care team.

·Advanced knowledge of nursing theory and practice, and/or additional specialized medical training, to provide expanded practice at a level generally acquired through completion of concentrated study and clinical internship leading to a Master's Degree.

·Analytical abilities necessary to obtain medical histories, conduct physical examinations, prepare complex treatment plans, and provide care for assigned patients with minimal guidance and direction.

What We Offer:

Our position offers variable scheduling. Off shift requirements (nights/weekends/holidays) are shared equally within the group. In addition, we offer a recruitment payment; relocation assistance, if qualified; CME reimbursement, and other great benefits.

Education:

·Completion of accredited NNP, PNP Acute Care Certification or PA.

Licensure:

·Current license for Advanced Practice in the state of Maine or pending license.

At MaineHealth, we recognize the value each team member brings to our organization. Total compensation packages may include, based on eligibility, recruitment payments, relocation assistance, shift differentials, productivity-based incentives, quality incentives and other premiums.

The pay range for this position at 1.00FTE/40 hrs is $140,910 to $182,354 annually, based on the candidate’s level of experience.

In addition to base pay, MaineHealth offers comprehensive benefits, recognition programs and career growth opportunities.

MaineHealth is a not-for-profit integrated health system whose vision is, “Working together so our communities are the healthiest in America.” MaineHealth consists of nine local health systems, a comprehensive behavioral health care network, diagnostic services, home health agencies, and 1,700 employed clinicians working together through the MaineHealth Medical Group. With approximately 22,000 care team members, MaineHealth provides preventive care, diagnosis and treatment to 1.1 million residents in Maine and New Hampshire. MaineHealth offers a Total Rewards package that includes comprehensive and competitive benefits, along with programs and resources to meet the diverse needs of our workforce.

To learn more about our system, please visit www.mainehealth.org and our benefits page.

For more information, please apply and/or contact Kelley Johnson, Physician & APP Recruiter at [email protected]

jobs.title: Nurse Practitioner - Pediatrics Acute Care
jobs.summary: Nurse Practitioner - Pediatrics Acute Care at Prisma Health Children's Hospital-Upstate. Setting: pediatric inpatient / hospitalist.
jobs.description:
Inspire health. Serve with compassion. Be the difference.

Job Summary

Working directly with Intensivists to provide care to a specific patient population within the guidelines of written protocols. Will be performing critical care procedures such as, but not limited to, intubation, arterial lines/central line insertion, chest tube placement and therapeutic bronchoscopy.

Accountabilities

• Patient evaluation: Assess patients by performing medical history and physical examination, including the medical, nursing, functional and financial conditions. Document all assessments in the patient medical record as appropriate.
• Ordering of tests: Order appropriate laboratory tests, x-rays, EKGs and diagnostic procedures based on assessment and follow-up as appropriate.
• Write Prescriptions and Orders: Write prescriptions/physician order under jointly developed protocols and practice guidelines.
• Patient Care: Manage care in collaboration with physicians and other clinical personnel. Provide consultation to colleagues and allied personnel.
• Rounds/ Documentation: Rounds on inpatients based on directions of the attending physician. Dictate and document patient history, physical exam and plans of care. Document admission and discharge notes when appropriate, ensuring that all documentation is clear, complete and legible.
• Invasive Procedures: Perform specific invasive procedures, within the scope of advanced practice nursing.
• Care improvement and evaluation: Evaluate the quality of care provided and identify opportunities for improvements in patient care and clinical operations.
• Research: Participate in research projects, papers or other publications.

Supervisory/Management Responsibilities

This is a non-management job that will report to a supervisor, manager, director or executive.

Minimum Requirements

Education - Master's Degree - Nursing; Nurse Practitioner Degree Emphasis or Program Certificate equivalent.

Experience - 3 years- Previous nursing experience in a critical care area such as ICU, CCU required. Some NP experience preferred but physicians will provide additional training.

Required Certifications/Registrations/Licenses

• NURSE PRACTITIONER - NLNP
• Official Recognition as a Nurse Practitioner in the state the team member is working
• Prescriptive Authority for the state in which the team member is working
• Controlled Substance license for the state in which the team member is working. Federal DEA license

Other Required Skills and Experience

• Clerical Testing
• Basic computer skills
• Word processing
• Mathematical skills
• Patient Equipment (Vitals, Suction, Defib)

Work Shift

Variable (United States of America)

Location

Patewood Outpt Ctr/Med Offices

jobs.department: 12-hour shifts, variable shifts, weekend and holidays required
jobs.summary: Neonatal - Full Time NP/PA at Atrium Health Levine Children's Brenner Children's Hospital. Setting: NICU / neonatology. Notable: relocation assistance.
jobs.description:
Explore an exciting opportunity with AHWFB's Neonatology Department as we eagerly welcome a skilled Neonatal Nurse Practitioner to join our dynamic inpatient team in Winston Salem, North Carolina.

What We Have to Offer:

• CME Reimbursement: Receive up to $2,500 and 5 additional PTO days/year for Continuing Medical Education.
• Work/Life Balance:12-hour shifts, variable shifts, weekend and holidays required
• Generous PTO: Accrual starts at 25 days/year, to be used for vacations, sickness, holidays, and personal matters.
• Relocation Assistance: Enjoy $7,500 in relocation assistance, paid within the first 30 days of employment.
• Career Growth & Stability: Experience a rewarding career with ample opportunities for advancement and stability, supported by a consistently high patient volume.
• A Rich Quality of Life: Indulge in a vibrant lifestyle within North Carolina's Piedmont Triad region, boasting an abundance of walking and biking trails, nationally acclaimed golf courses, active arts communities, tantalizing Southern cuisine, and an array of artisan craft breweries and wineries.

Where You'll Work:

At Brenner Children's Hospital, our Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICU) are integral to our commitment to providing exceptional care. Delivering top-tier Level II, III, and IV services, our expansive NICU serves over 700 infants annually from across the South. Our team is a passionate group of healthcare professionals, including skilled Neonatal Nurse Practitioners (NNPs), who specialize in treating a wide range of congenital and acquired conditions. By joining our team, you'll be part of a dedicated and compassionate community committed to providing the highest level of care to the most vulnerable patients

What You'll Do:

As a valued member of our NICU team, the NNP will play a key role in team-focused patient care, conducting thorough examinations and evaluations in medical setting. Responsibilities include:

Utilizes advanced knowledge and skills to provide nursing and selected medical procedures for neonates and infants

Communicates and collaborates with appropriate members of the health care team, including patient families

Works to improve the quality of care provided to neonates

Advances the care of neonates through participation in and application of the research process. Shares knowledge on a formal and informal basis with interdisciplinary team as relates to specialty area

Ensures the continuous quality of professional services by maintaining updated knowledge and skills

Maintaining current and valid licensure with the State Board of Nursing to provide continuous nursing services to prevent the spread of bloodborne and/or airborne disease(s)

Ensures age/developmentally appropriate patient care is provided in accordance with Age-Specific Care Guidelines for the specific age groups served

Performs other related duties incidental to the work described herein

The clinician functions under the regulatory mandate from their respective licensing organization (North Carolina Board of Nursing) with departmental specific credentialing from the institution.

Nurse Practitioner (NNP) Requirements:

• Graduation from accredited Nurse Practitioner Master's Program, Master's degree or higher required
• Current North Carolina Board of Nursing Registered Nurse and Nurse Practitioner license
• Board certified as a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner
• Welcoming to new and experienced NNP providers
• BCLS, PALS and NRP required

Where You'll Live:

The picturesque cities of North Carolina's Piedmont Triad region are ranked among US News & World Report's Top 50 Best Places to Live and Top 40 Best Places to Retire in 2023. This includes:

• Affordable Living: Enjoy a family-friendly and affordable area, with housing costs 31% below the national average.
• Great Schools: Access to top-notch educational institutions and high-ranking school systems provide excellent opportunities for personal and academic growth.
• Vibrant Neighborhoods: Join a regional population of 1.6 million residents, where lively downtowns and family-orientated neighborhoods create a warm and inviting atmosphere.

jobs.title: Pediatric CVICU- Full Time NP/PA
jobs.department: Rotating shifts, days - 11.5 hours dayshift and 14 hour night shift; weekends/holidays required
jobs.summary: Pediatric CVICU- Full Time NP/PA at Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital. Setting: PICU / pediatric critical care. Notable: nights.
jobs.description:
The APP will function independently in the inpatient hospital in collaboration with a supervising physician and other members of a multidisciplinary team for cardiac surgical and non-surgical patients in the CVICU. These patients include but are not limited to complex neonatal repairs, VAD, ECMO and transplant patients.

Essential Functions:

Functions independently to perform age-appropriate, disease-specific history and physical examination of complex acute, critical, and chronic advanced heart failure patients.

Rounds daily with interdisciplinary team

Manages care and treatment plan as the front-line provider for patients

Orders and interprets diagnostic and therapeutic tests, including laboratory and radiologic

Prescribes appropriate pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic treatment modalities

Monitors the effectiveness of interventions

Documents all patient encounters, records observations, interventions, and actions in a medically appropriate manner in the patient’s electronic medical record

Collaborates with members of the multidisciplinary team including, but not limited to: physicians, nurses, medical assistants, social workers, pharmacists, dieticians

Performs chest tube removals, pacer wire removals and pediatric ICU procedures including chest tube insertion, central and arterial line access and intubations

Attends, participates, and contributes to group/practice meetings, quality improvement, and policy and procedure development efforts when requested.

Min Work standards- 1880 hours per year- shifts are varied with days, nights and weekends split amongst group excluding nocturnist APPs.

Must be approved to practice as a Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant in the state of North and South Carolina. Eligible for prescriptive authority application through the Board of Nursing or Medical Board in North and South Carolina. Must have or be eligible for a DEA license. BLS for Healthcare Provider from AHA required with expiration date greater than 90 days from date of beginning practice. Demonstrates appropriate critical thinking, interpersonal skills, and the ability to prioritize and concentrate. 2+ years of experience as an APP in a relevant field preferred.

Atrium Health Levine Children’s Congenital Heart Center, established in 2010, is currently ranked #7 in the country for Best Children’s Hospital for Cardiology & Heart Surgery by U.S. News and World Report. Our comprehensive services include cardiac imaging, diagnostic and interventional catheterization, invasive electrophysiology, dedicated cardiovascular intensive care staff, and regional referral programs in heart failure/transplantation, adult congenital heart disease, and fetal echocardiography. Our state-of-the-art two lab cardiac catheterization and electrophysiology suite and new outpatient office complex is filled with dedicated staffing and is designed to treat all patients from fetal cardiology to ACHD. Our comprehensive Cardiac Neurodevelopment program provides a multitude of specialty services to our congenital heart patients in the same office suite. Participation in investigator initiated and multi-center industry sponsored studies is ongoing within the Heart Center, with the support of an active clinical research department

Levine Children’s Hospital (LCH) is a state-of-the-art facility in beautiful Charlotte, North Carolina. LCH has 11 floors and 258 inpatient beds, including on-site PICU and CVICU covered 24/7 by in-house intensivists, Progressive Care Unit, Inpatient Observation Unit, Pediatric Rehab Unit, and Pediatric Emergency Department. We are committed to being the region’s leading provider of pediatric health care services.

Our Impact:

Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health have come together to do more, be better and go faster to help more people live well. Together, we will deliver the best health outcomes and make care more accessible and affordable for all.

Headquartered in Charlotte and powered by 150,000 talented teammates – including the best and brightest physicians, nurses, researchers and faculty – we are poised to improve safety and health outcomes, advance health equity and accelerate medical breakthroughs, with Wake Forest University School of Medicine as our academic core.

jobs.title: Peds GI APP- Full Time NP/PA
jobs.summary: Peds GI APP- Full Time NP/PA at Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital. Setting: mixed settings.
jobs.description:
If it’s possible, you will find it at Atrium Health—the leading community-focused academic healthcare system serving North Carolina and South Carolina. We invite APPs to discover all that we can do when we bring healing hearts, inquisitive minds and progressive visionaries together in our Levine Children’s Hospital team in Charlotte.

The Division of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition at Atrium Health Levine Children's is seeking an advanced practice practitioner to join our growing outpatient pediatric GI practice. You will work with a talented and collegial group of 14 physicians and 5 advanced practice providers, 5 registered dietitians, 2 dedicated pediatric psychologists, 2 licensed clinical social workers, and an outstanding nursing team and support staff. The practice is based at the Levine Children's Specialty Center on the campus of Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital, with multiple satellite offices throughout the greater Charlotte region. Our division provides comprehensive services for all children's digestive conditions and has been ranked in the US News & World Report top 25 programs in the country for the last 3 years.

LCH has repeatedly been ranked among the Best Children's Hospitals in the nation by U.S. News & World Report, most recently in seven pediatric specialties for 2024-2025, including Urology, Cardiology and Heart Surgery, Gastroenterology and GI Surgery, Nephrology, Cancer, Orthopedics, and Pulmonology and Lung Surgery. The growing academic department brings exciting opportunities for innovative patient care, team-based care models, teaching, and research.

Position:

This APP position will be a hybrid role to include both inpatient and outpatient coverage, offering a varied patient population. When outpatient, the APP will have their own clinic template with a major focus on long-term management of our large population of enterally tube fed patients (i.e gastrostomy tube, gastrojejunostomy tube), and patients with general gastroenterology conditions including gastroesophageal reflux disease, constipation, abdominal pain, failure to thrive, and milk protein intolerance. Our outpatient APPs also work collaboratively with our inpatient APPs to ensure excellent hospital follow-up for patients needing our services. While inpatient, the APP will see hospitalized patients in collaboration with the gastroenterology attending physicians. The inpatient GI service is primarily a consultation service offering recommendations to the primary team (general pediatrics, PICU, Cardiology, NICU or hematology/oncology), but at times it has primary patients. The candidate will have excellent mentorship from current experienced GI APP's and supportive supervising physicians.

This position has no nighttime call or weekend responsibilities. There are also opportunities for involvement in clinical research and quality improvement projects.

jobs.summary: NICU (Weekender) - Full Time NP/PA at Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital. Setting: NICU / neonatology.
jobs.description:
MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Clinical responsibilities:

Assesses, diagnoses, and determines/alters treatment and management plans appropriate for age, acuity and clinical condition. This includes ordering, performing, and interpreting appropriate diagnostic studies and prescription of pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic interventions and therapies.

Manages conditions based on clinical indication, evidence-based care, cost effectiveness, and assessment of risks/benefits and alternatives.

Provides health promotion, disease prevention and disease management counseling and education of patients and families.

Manages patients as part of an interdisciplinary team and within scope of practice. Seeks physician or other healthcare team member consultation or referrals as appropriate. Escalates need for more emergent or specialized care when necessary.

Maintains accurate, complete, concise, and timely documentation in the electronic medical record. Substantiates and submits professional services consistent with compliant coding and billing practices.

Facilitates consistent, coordinated care and clear communication among all members of the healthcare team and/or health or community agencies.

Performs office or hospital procedures in accordance with specialty practice, competency and granted privileges (where applicable).

Other responsibilities:

jobs.description:
The Lisa Dean Moseley Foundation Institute for Cancer and Blood Disorders at Nemours Children’s Hospital, Delaware is seeking a Pediatric Oncology & Cellular Therapies APP (Advanced Practice Nurse or Physician Assistant) with special interest in the inpatient management of both pediatric oncology and hematology patients inclusive of those undergoing stem cell transplantation/cellular therapies and to join the team!

This is a full-time opportunity to join a thriving Hematology/Oncology division in Delaware’s only free-standing children’s hospital. Primary responsibilities will include the inpatient clinical management of children with malignant hematological disorders, solid tumors, sickle cell disease and patients receiving stem cell transplant and cellular therapies. The pediatric hematology/oncology APRN/PA in this position will work collaboratively with the inpatient hematology/oncology provider team (attendings, advanced practice providers, fellows & residents) to provide seamless patient/family centered healthcare. Additional responsibilities for this front-line clinician include providing coverage for the outpatient pediatric oncology, stem cell transplant/cellular therapies and hematology patient populations as needed.

Highlights of the pediatric hematology/oncology/transplant/cellular therapy program include a supportive and collaborative group of 12 pediatric hematologists/oncologists and 11 advanced practice providers along with dedicated oncology nurses, psychologists, child life specialists, nutritionists, physical therapists, nurse navigators, and social workers. The program is a member of the Children’s Oncology Group and one of the top enrollers of patients in the NCI Community Oncology Research Program (NCORP).

Essential duties and responsibilities will include:

Primary inpatient management of both pediatric hematology and oncology patients including those undergoing stem cell transplant/cellular therapies. Provide continuity of care specific to disease evaluation, chemotherapy/immunotherapy, supportive care management throughout the patient’s treatment course in conjunction with an attending pediatric hematologist/oncologist. Demonstrates a commitment to patient safety in ordering chemotherapy/immunotherapy and supportive care medication/therapies using a computerized order entry system.

Requirements:

• Master's/Doctorate as applicable in correlation with Nursing or Physician Assistant program
• Pediatric Advanced Practice Registered Nurse-Acute Care Certified OR Physician Assistant (PA-C)
• Pediatric Oncology and/or Transplant/Cellular Therapy experience highly preferred.

CPR-BLS Certification required at the time of appointment.

Nemours offers its Associates a competitive salary and a robust benefits package that includes relocation, health/life/dental/vision for Associates and their dependents, a wellness program, CME, 403(b) with employer match, licensure and dues allowance, tuition reimbursement, loan forgiveness program, legal plan, adoption assistance and many other benefit options. If you’re looking for a position that will allow you to enjoy a work-life balance, have an opportunity for professional growth, and focus on pediatric care, this is the opportunity for you.

#LI-MR1

Nemours Children's Health is an internationally recognized pediatric health system serving more than 1.7 million patient encounters each year. We deliver care across six states through two freestanding children’s hospitals — Nemours Children's Hospital, Delaware and Nemours Children's Hospital, Florida — along with a network of more than 80 primary, urgent, and specialty care practices and more than 40 hospital partnerships.

Backed by the Nemours Foundation and Alfred I. duPont Trust, our $1.7B nonprofit system is dedicated to improving children's health through clinical care, research, education, advocacy, and prevention. Our Whole Child Health approach focuses equally on prevention and treatment, partnering with communities to help every child thrive.

Inclusion and belonging guide our strategy and growth. We are committed to culturally relevant care, reducing health disparities, and fostering an environment where every associate, patient, and family feels supported and valued.

Learn more at Nemours.org.

Overview

About the Role

The Advanced Practice Nurse (APN) is a skilled health provider who through a written collaborative practice agreement with a physician is credentialed through the Medical Staff Office. Description:

Nurse Practitioner - Infant Cardiac ICU- Full Time- Rotating

Picture 5,500 nurses practicing at the top academic medical center in New York City. For Nurse Practitioners, New York-Presbyterian represents the ultimate career opportunity – the chance to make a difference. Transform your career as Nurse Practitioner within the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at New York-Presbyterian/Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital. Educate colleagues and Ivy League students, and engage in our Advanced Practice Registered Nurse Council that works to improve workflow, patient experience, employee satisfaction, timeliness, quality and safety for patients and staff.

The Infant Cardiac ICU is globally the first and only Neonatal Intensive Care Unit dedicated to the care of newborns and young infants with congenital heart disease (CHD) from birth, to when they go for their surgery, up to their discharge.

Fifty years since creating the APGAR score for newborn evaluation, NYP is among the nation’s best for neonatal care, and a Regional Perinatal Network hub. We care for the tiniest, most critically ill patients - relying on our dedicated nurses' expertise.

jobs.description:
Pediatric Nurse Practitioner (Neurorehabilitation). Vacancy ID 13340. Position Category: Nursing. Location: 801 N. Broadway, Baltimore, MD. Regular Full Time, 32.00 hours. Salary USD $83,483.00 - $149,453.00 /Yr.

Overview: The nurse practitioner is a healthcare provider on a multidisciplinary team, providing comprehensive care to patients, educating them, and intervening in acute or chronic illness. The nurse practitioner practices under Kennedy Krieger Institute and departmental guidelines and Maryland Nurse Practitioner regulations and the Nurse Practice Act, with privileges granted by the Institute's Medical Board and reviewed annually.

Responsibilities: 1. Conducts comprehensive or episodic health assessments of patients and families, including psychosocial, cognitive and personal strengths and limitations, with an emphasis on wellness. 2. Performs health screenings, orders and interprets tests, establishes medical and nursing diagnoses, and manages treatment and follow-up plans. 3. Assesses chronic health problems and refers patients to an attending or primary provider when appropriate. 4. Collaborates with other professionals on care plans for children and adolescents. 5. Documents health assessment data to maintain, coordinate and expedite services. 6. Manages own time, professional relationships and interactions. 7. Educates caregivers and team members on medications, illness management and disease prevention, and teaches children and adolescents about healthy practices. 8. Develops, conducts and evaluates in-service and continuing education programs. 9. Pursues ongoing professional development and clinical currency. 10. Participates in nursing research and applies scientific knowledge to practice. 11. Serves on department, unit and hospital committees as assigned. 12. Serves as a clinical preceptor for nursing students, including nurse practitioner candidates. 13. Advocates for children and adolescents with developmental disabilities in health, community and school settings. 14. Participates in developing and implementing a quality assurance program.

Qualifications: Unencumbered RN licensure and Maryland nurse practitioner certification, maintained continuously. DEA registration and Maryland CDS registration, maintained continuously. National certification in the area of specialty from a recognized certifying board (e.g., ANCC or Pediatric Nursing Certification Board). Education: Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) required. Experience: Minimum two years of related clinical nursing experience.

jobs.title: Advanced Practice Provider (NNP/PA/APP) Neonatal Critical Care (NICU)
jobs.summary: Advanced Practice Provider (NNP/PA/APP) Neonatal Critical Care (NICU) at UVA Health Children's. Setting: NICU / neonatology. Notable: new grad friendly, nights, relocation assistance.
jobs.description:
Deliver lifesaving care at the highest level of neonatal medicine within a rapidly expanding Level IV NICU. This role places you at the center of complex, high acuity care where your clinical expertise directly shapes outcomes for the most vulnerable patients and their families.

As an Advanced Practice Provider in UVA Health’s NICU, you will practice at the top of your license in a collaborative, academically driven environment. This is an opportunity to build deep neonatal expertise, perform advanced procedures, and grow your career in a unit experiencing significant expansion and investment.

The Role

In this high acuity NICU setting, no two shifts are the same. You’ll care for critically ill neonates while working alongside an interdisciplinary team committed to evidence‑based, family centered care. The unit’s pace is dynamic, the clinical complexity is high, and the impact is profound.

A typical experience in this role includes:

• Managing premature and critically ill neonates, including complex congenital cardiac conditions requiring surgical intervention
• Performing advanced procedures such as:
• Intubation
• Umbilical line placement
• Central line insertion
• Chest tube placement
• Lumbar punctures
• Utilizing Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) for line placement and lung diagnostics
• Collaborating closely with neonatologists, nurses, respiratory therapists, and surgical teams
• Engaging in family-centered care, supporting and guiding families through critical moments
• Practicing in a high-acuity, fast-paced environment that demands clinical excellence and adaptability

Schedule & Work Style:

• Full-time: 13 shifts per 4-week block (12-hour shifts)
• Rotating days and nights
• Self-scheduling model designed to support work-life balance

You will be supported by a structured onboarding experience tailored to your background, with individualized orientation timelines and strong mentorship to ensure success at every stage of your career.

https://app.uvahs.org/

Advanced Practice Provider Scope of Practice:

Clinical

• Provides expert evidence-based, top-of-scope care in their clinical practice
• Acts as part of a specialty team, collaborating with other clinicians as appropriate
• Provides health education to patients
• Maintains accurate, timely, and thorough documentation
• Ensures compliance with institutional and regulatory standards

Leadership

• Supports development of best practices and protocols in specialty
• Serves on committees and workgroups to enhance patient care
• Provides education to learners in the clinical space
• Mentors new team members

Administration

• Contributes to clinical quality improvement work
• Participates in professional governance through the APP Council
• Attends team development meetings at local and departmental levels

Professional

• Adheres to ASPIRE values in all professional interactions
• Maintains appropriate licenses, certifications, and specialty training competencies
• Participates in local, state, and national professional organizations

Background checks and pre-employment health screenings will be conducted on all new hires prior to employment. All safety-sensitive positions with direct patient interaction also require a drug screen.

Why UVA Health

UVA Health offers the rare combination of academic medicine, advanced clinical capability, and a supportive team culture, all within a health system that is actively expanding and investing in neonatal care.

This NICU is part of a top-ranked children’s hospital and operates as a Level IV referral center, delivering the most advanced neonatal care available. You will join during a transformative period of growth, with the NICU expanding significantly to meet rising demand for complex care.

What sets this opportunity apart:

• High-acuity Level IV NICU environment with ECMO capabilities and exposure to the most complex neonatal cases
• Major expansion initiative, growing capacity and creating opportunities for career advancement and leadership
• Strong team-oriented culture that supports both experienced clinicians and new graduates
• Robust professional development pathways, including opportunities in:
• Clinical specialization
• Education and mentorship
• Research and academic involvement
• Quality improvement and leadership
• Highly individualized onboarding and training, including transition-to-practice programs for new graduates
• Commitment to work-life balance through flexible, self-scheduled shifts
• A culture that values continuous learning, resilience, and collaboration

Relocation assistance may be available for qualified candidates.

Why People Love Living in Charlottesville

Charlottesville offers an exceptional quality of life that makes it easy to balance a demanding clinical career with personal wellbeing. Nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, the area is known for its natural beauty, vibrant food and wine scene, and rich cultural offerings. Residents enjoy easy access to hiking, outdoor recreation, and scenic landscapes, while also benefiting from a welcoming, community-oriented atmosphere. With a strong sense of place and a pace that supports both professional fulfillment and personal renewal, Charlottesville is an ideal home for healthcare professionals seeking balance and connection.

Monitor patient progress and adjust treatment plans as needed.

Educate patients and families regarding health conditions, treatment plans, nutrition, growth, development, and disease prevention.

jobs.description:
Your passion belongs at UNC Health. Join more than 56,000 teammates working together to improve the health and well-being of the communities we serve across North Carolina.

Position Summary

The UNC Department of Pediatrics, Division of Pediatric Pulmonology, is seeking a part-time Nurse Practitioner (NP) to join the UNC Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD) Interdisciplinary Care Program. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing multidisciplinary program dedicated to improving the care and long-term outcomes of infants and children with BPD and other respiratory complications of prematurity.

The UNC BPD Program provides interdisciplinary care for medically complex infants and children with BPD across the continuum from the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) through childhood. The program brings together specialists from pediatric pulmonology, neonatology, cardiology, nutrition, developmental therapies, respiratory therapy, social work, and other disciplines to provide coordinated, evidence-based care. Through a recently funded program expansion, the team is developing a comprehensive outpatient interdisciplinary BPD program while expanding education, consultation, and outreach to healthcare partners across North Carolina.

The APP will serve as a key clinical member of the BPD team and will work closely with pediatric pulmonologists with expertise in BPD, with opportunities for mentorship and professional development in the care of infants and children with chronic lung disease of prematurity. The position will also support inpatient pulmonary consultation for children with BPD and participate in program development, care coordination, education, quality improvement, and outreach activities.

BPD Program Responsibilities

Specific responsibilities will include:

• Provide outpatient evaluation and longitudinal management of established infants and children with BPD and other respiratory complications of prematurity, in collaboration with pediatric pulmonologists.
• Participate in multidisciplinary BPD clinics, coordinating care with neonatology, cardiology, nutrition, developmental specialists, social work, respiratory therapy, and other disciplines.
• Assist with inpatient pediatric pulmonary consultation and longitudinal care planning for infants and children with BPD, including transition planning from the NICU to outpatient pulmonary care.
• Manage common BPD-related outpatient needs, including supplemental oxygen and respiratory equipment, respiratory medications, symptom management, diagnostic testing, and ongoing assessment of respiratory status.
• Provide education and counseling to patients and families regarding BPD, respiratory therapies, home oxygen and equipment, medications, and anticipatory guidance.
• Participate in multidisciplinary BPD team meetings and contribute to development and implementation of standardized clinical pathways, protocols, and evidence-based care practices.
• Support quality improvement and program evaluation activities, including patient outcome tracking and development of the BPD patient registry.
• Participate in education and outreach activities for healthcare professionals within UNC and at collaborating hospitals and community practices across North Carolina.

About the UNC BPD Program

UNC Children's currently cares for more than 100 new infants with BPD each year and has developed an interdisciplinary inpatient BPD program for infants with moderate-to-severe lung disease. The program is now expanding to establish comprehensive interdisciplinary outpatient care, strengthen transitions from the NICU to home, and increase access to BPD expertise throughout North Carolina.

The BPD Interdisciplinary Care and Outreach Program is supported by a grant from The Duke Endowment and is designed to establish a sustainable model of coordinated BPD care across inpatient, outpatient, and community settings. The program is partnering with hospitals and healthcare professionals across North Carolina to expand access to BPD expertise, develop educational resources and standardized care practices, and improve long-term outcomes for children affected by prematurity.

Preferred Qualifications

• Licensed as an Advanced Practice Provider (Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant, etc.) in the state of North Carolina
• Prior experience in pediatric pulmonology, neonatology/NICU (including experience as a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner), complex care, pediatric critical care, or the care of medically complex infants and children is preferred but not required.
• Interest in longitudinal care of infants and children with chronic lung disease and medical complexity.
• Strong communication and collaborative skills and an interest in interdisciplinary team-based care.

Interest in clinical program development, quality improvement, patient/family education, and/or community outreach is desirable.

Have you considered a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner career with UNC Health? We are reaching out to share an exciting opportunity with you! The individual selected for this position will function as a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner (NNP) delivering critical care medical management in the Newborn Critical Care Center based at the North Carolina Children’s Hospital, the delivery rooms of the North Carolina Women’s Hospital, components of the UNC Hospitals, as well as the brand-new North Carolina Surgical Hospital. The practitioner works in a multi-disciplinary, academic environment and interacts at all professional levels (including students, residents, fellows, faculty and staff) of medical, surgical, nursing, respiratory therapy, and other medical allied health professionals.

The NCCC underwent an expansion in September 2024, opening 22 single patient rooms, including 2 spacious twin rooms, on the 6thfloor of the Children’s Hospital.

Become part of an inclusive organization with over 40,000 teammates, whose mission is to improve the health and well-being of the unique communities we serve.

Where you work is as important as where you play. Nestled in the Blue Ridge Mountains, Western North Carolina is not only a beautiful place, but a dynamic region filled with natural resources, a variety of cultural and educational opportunities, and some of the highest quality health care in the country. Physicians and medical professionals have settled here, drawn by the exceptional beauty and quality of life in Hendersonville.

Hendersonville is unique in having the feel of small town America, yet is geographically situated within convenient driving distance of the urban areas of Asheville, NC, Greenville, SC, and only a few hours from Atlanta, GA and Charlotte, NC. Nature is always close by with nearly twenty national, state, county and city parks, recreational areas and forests, many within of just outside the city limits of Hendersonville. Henderson County is ideally located for exploring festivals, recreational activities, historical sites, golf courses, family activities, and a variety of restaurants with high quality public schools and private schools.

UNC Health Pardee is a not-for-profit health care system that was founded in 1953 and is managed by UNC Health Care. It is the first hospital in the Carolinas to be accredited with the International Organization for Standardization for quality health care standards.

We are a licensed for 222 acute care beds and are the second-largest employer in Henderson County. We have several locations separate from our main campus, including a comprehensive physician practice network, multiple urgent care locations and five orthopedic clinics.

The practitioner will normally work rotating 12-24 hour shifts to include weekend assignments and night call. Per Diem duty time will be maintained over any given scheduling period. The Specialty Care Nursery (Level 2) at Nash UNC Health Care is located within the Women’s Center, a 47,048-square-foot facility opened in May 2016 and designed with input from mother-baby experts, community members, and new parents. The Women’s Center features:

• Six labor and delivery suites with private bathrooms
• A dedicated cesarean section suite and spacious recovery room
• Sixteen mother–baby postpartum rooms with private bathrooms
• A large, modern Special Care Nursery

The Specialty Care Unit includes twelve private infant rooms with accommodation for family members, including sleeping space, private bathrooms, and access to hot meals. Family presence and participation are encouraged. The unit provides care for intermediate-level neonates and stable growing premature infants. Services include oxygen therapy, continuous monitoring, IV therapy, phototherapy, antibiotics, and OG/NG feedings. Monitoring capabilities include central cardiac/respiratory monitoring, apnea/bradycardia monitoring, pulse oximetry, blood pressure, glucose, and thermoregulation.

Rocky Mount is located in Eastern North Carolina at the intersection of US 64 and I‑95, approximately 50 miles from Raleigh and RDU Airport. The region offers low cost of living and convenient access to beaches (120 miles) and mountain destinations (190 miles). Residents enjoy excellent work–life balance with local access to dining, lakes, parks, trails, performing arts, outdoor concerts, sports complexes, and family-friendly activities. Home to NC Wesleyan College, Rocky Mount is within an hour of NC State University, Duke University, East Carolina University, and UNC‑Chapel Hill.

jobs.description:
UVA Health Children’s is seeking an Advanced Practice Provider to join Pediatric Gastroenterology with a focus on children with feeding difficulties and gastrostomy tubes. This newly created position will improve access and continuity across inpatient and outpatient settings while providing specialized support for children and families with feeding and nutritional needs.

The APP will work closely with Pediatric Gastroenterology physicians and APPs, Nutrition, Pediatric Surgery, Complex Care, and other pediatric specialists. This is a Monday-Friday position with a combination of inpatient and outpatient responsibilities and no routine weekend coverage.

The Role

Responsibilities will include:

• Evaluate and manage children with feeding difficulties and gastrostomy-related needs across inpatient and outpatient settings.
• Provide follow-up care after gastrostomy placement and ongoing management for children with gastrostomy tubes.
• Perform gastrostomy tube changes and assess tube-site and skin concerns.
• Provide education and support to patients and caregivers regarding gastrostomy management and care.
• Collaborate with gastroenterologists and nutritionists to develop and coordinate individualized feeding and nutritional plans.
• Coordinate care with Pediatric Surgery, Complex Care, and other pediatric specialists as appropriate.
• Develop an independent patient schedule as clinical knowledge and autonomy grow.
• Help improve access, continuity, and transitions between inpatient and outpatient care.

This position is well suited for an APP with a strong pediatric clinical foundation who enjoys patient and family education, multidisciplinary care, and developing longitudinal relationships with children and families. Pediatric GI, nutrition, feeding, or gastrostomy experience is preferred; new graduates with strong clinical preparation are encouraged to apply.

Cover letter preferred with application.

jobs.description:
Advanced Practice Provider (APP) – LCSW or LPC

NICU & PICU | UVA Health Children’s | Charlottesville, Virginia

Support families when it matters most.

At UVA Health Children’s, pediatric critical care is not just about advanced medicine. It is about meeting families at their most vulnerable moments with compassion, clinical expertise, and unwavering partnership. We are seeking an experienced Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) or Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) to join our Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) in an Advanced Practice Provider role designed for clinicians who want meaningful autonomy, interdisciplinary respect, and the opportunity to shape how behavioral health is delivered in a high acuity pediatric environment.

This role is ideal for clinicians who value autonomy in clinical judgment, thrive in medically complex settings, and are energized by building and evolving care models within an academic children’s hospital.

The Role

This APP behavioral health position is embedded directly within UVA Health Children’s NICU and PICU, supporting families of infants and children facing critical illness, trauma, and prolonged hospitalization. You will function as an autonomous clinician while working shoulder‑to‑shoulder with pediatric intensivists, neonatologists, nurses, and subspecialists.

In this role, you will:

Maintain clinical autonomy to assess, diagnose, and deliver psychotherapy in a fast paced pediatric critical care setting

Provide individual, couples, and family therapy, helping caregivers cope with grief, trauma, uncertainty, and complex medical decision-making

Serve as a consistent behavioral health presence for families experiencing extended ICU stays

Collaborate daily with a highly interdisciplinary care team, contributing psychosocial insight that directly informs care planning

Help develop and refine behavioral health workflows within the NICU and PICU as the service continues to evolve

What an average day looks like:

Participating in interdisciplinary rounds where psychosocial dynamics are integrated into treatment planning

Providing real-time therapy and crisis support in response to acute family needs

Partnering with physicians and nursing leaders around communication strategies, ethical stressors, and family support

Balancing scheduled sessions with responsive, bedside care

The pace is dynamic, the work is emotionally meaningful, and the impact is tangible every day.

Background checks and pre-employment health screenings will be conducted on all new hires prior to employment. All safety-sensitive positions with direct patient interaction also require a drug screen.

Why UVA Health

UVA Health Children’s is part of a nationally recognized academic health system anchored by a Level I Trauma Center, a Level IV NICU, and one of the most advanced pediatric critical care programs in the region. UVA Health Children’s is consistently recognized as the #1 children’s hospital in Virginia, supported by Magnet recognized nursing excellence and a deeply collaborative culture. Pediatric Critical Care at UVA Health Children’s offers:

Comprehensive care for critically ill children from birth through young adulthood, including acute, chronic, and medically complex conditions

Dedicated medical and cardiac PICU teams with access to advanced therapies such as extracorporeal support, congenital heart surgery, heart failure care, and transplant services

A deeply interdisciplinary model where behavioral health, medical teams, and family centered care are fully integrated

Strong academic infrastructure with opportunities to contribute to program development, quality improvement, and innovation within pediatric critical care

Why this role matters:

Behavioral health is a strategic and valued component of pediatric critical care at UVA

You will have a voice in shaping how families are supported across the NICU and PICU continuum

The environment supports professional judgment, collaboration, and clinical growth within academic medicine

Relocation assistance may be available for qualified candidates.

Why People Love Living in Charlottesville

Charlottesville offers a rare combination of intellectual energy, natural beauty, and balance that resonates strongly with healthcare professionals. Nestled at the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, the area provides easy access to hiking, cycling, wineries, and outdoor recreation, alongside a vibrant food scene, arts community, and strong public schools. The pace of life allows clinicians to recharge outside of work while remaining part of a close‑knit, purpose driven community.

jobs.description:
Join a growing pediatric subspecialty practice where your clinical judgment, procedural curiosity, and commitment to children and families can make a direct impact every day.

UVA Health is seeking an Advanced Practice Provider to join Pediatric Otolaryngology, a busy, high-volume pediatric ENT practice within an academic medical center. This is an opportunity to build deep specialty expertise, work closely with pediatric ENT surgeons and APP colleagues, and help children and families navigate common and complex otolaryngology needs with confidence, compassion, and clinical excellence.

The Role

In this ambulatory APP role, you will evaluate and manage pediatric patients with a range of otolaryngology conditions in a collaborative, specialty-focused clinic environment. You will be part of a team that values thoughtful assessment, efficient clinical flow, strong communication, and patient and family-centered care.

This position is especially well-suited for an APP who enjoys pediatric care, wants to grow within a subspecialty, and is energized by a practice setting that combines high patient volume, procedural learning, and close partnership with surgeons. This is primarily a daytime, ambulatory clinic opportunity, with future potential to evolve into a more hybrid role that may include inpatient responsibilities alongside another APP.

In an average day, you may:

Independently evaluate pediatric ENT patients, perform histories and physical examinations, and develop treatment plans.

Diagnose and treat common pediatric otolaryngology conditions in the ambulatory clinic setting.

Identify patients who may require surgical intervention and help facilitate timely progression to surgery when appropriate.

Provide pre-operative and post-operative education and management for patients and families.

Collaborate with attending surgeons, APP colleagues, referring providers, and multidisciplinary team members.

Perform and interpret diagnostic tests and office-based procedures within scope.

Learn and develop procedural skills such as nasal cauterizations, foreign body removals, and other common ENT procedures.

Maintain accurate, timely EHR documentation and support clinic throughput, productivity, and quality goals.

Contribute to quality improvement and the continued growth of the pediatric ENT service line.

The Nemours Cardiac Center of the Children’s Hospital in Wilmington, Delaware is looking for a qualified Pediatric Acute Care Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant- Inpatient Telemetry Cardiac Center! This role is a full-time nocturnist role, including weekend, and holiday availability.

The Advanced Practice Provider (APP) in the Cardiac Inpatient Telemetry Unit plays a vital role in delivering high-quality, patient-centered care in a dynamic environment. In collaboration with physicians, APPs, consultants, nurses, and other healthcare professionals, the APP will provide specialized care to critically ill cardiac patients.

This role requires comprehensive care for cardiac surgical patients during both the pre-operative and post-operative periods as well as providing care for non-surgical patients. The APP is required to perform medical histories and physical exams as well as interpret laboratory and diagnostic testing data to inform clinical decisions. Additionally, the APP will be required to develop and implement patient care management plans, including prescribing medications and other medical therapies.

This role is a full-time nocturnist role, including weekend, and holiday availability. Applicants should be highly motivated to join a high-functioning multidisciplinary team. Excellent written and verbal communication skills are required.

For confidential Consideration

Apply online today! Or send your resume via email to Megan.Roberts@nemours.org.

jobs.description:
UVA Health Primary Care Culpeper is seeking an experienced and autonomously licensed, Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) to provide outpatient behavioral health services within a collaborative primary care setting. This full-time virtual position offers a four-day workweek (4 x 10-hour shifts) with no inpatient responsibilities. Experience with ages 5 and up. For this position, there would be some required onsite meetings, collaboration and networking to ensure the role is fully integrated with the clinic teams and workflows. However, patient visits would be conducted virtually.

Responsible for provision of Advanced Practice Provider services, including assessment and management of patients across all clinical settings, (examples: ambulatory clinic, hospital, assisted living facility, skilled nursing facility/nursing home, ambulatory surgery center, and community settings), within the scope of licensing, training, and credentialing dependent on specialty.

Virtual Delivery Requirements
• Must reside in Virginia and deliver all care from within the Commonwealth
• Reliable high-speed internet required for video-based patient care
• Computer equipment will be provided
• Private, confidential workspace suitable for clinical telehealth
Schedule
• 32 patient-facing hours per week plus 8 hours of administrative time (total 40 hours)
• Schedule could include weekend and/or evening coverage as needed and based on patient needs.
• Flexibility is essential to success in this role.

Position Highlights

• No hospital call or inpatient coverage
• Integrated behavioral health model within a primary care practice
• Collaborative support from primary care providers, nursing, and care management teams

Key Responsibilities

• Conduct comprehensive psychiatric evaluations and diagnostic assessments for adolescents and adults.
• Diagnose and treat a broad range of mental health conditions, including depression, anxiety, ADHD, PTSD, bipolar disorder, and other psychiatric disorders.
• Develop individualized treatment plans utilizing evidence-based medication management and therapeutic interventions.
• Prescribe, adjust, and monitor psychotropic medications in accordance with Virginia regulations and clinical best practices.
• Provide ongoing follow-up care, including symptom management, treatment monitoring, and medication education.
• Collaborate closely with primary care providers to support integrated patient care and address behavioral health needs within the primary care setting.
• Coordinate referrals to specialty behavioral health services, counseling, substance use treatment, and community resources as appropriate.
• Maintain accurate and timely documentation in the electronic medical record.
• Participate in quality improvement initiatives and contribute to a patient-centered, team-based care environment.

Qualifications

• Master's or Doctoral degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program.
• Board certification as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP).
• Current or eligible Virginia Nurse Practitioner and Registered Nurse licensure.
• DEA registration and prescriptive authority eligibility.
• Minimum of 3 years of psychiatric practice experience.
• Ability to practice independently and manage a diverse outpatient psychiatric patient panel.

COMPENSATION

• Tiered base salary plus a productivity (wRVU)-based incentive model.
• Base salary is determined by years of APP experience:
• 0–5 years of experience: $105,000 base salary
• More than 5 years up to 10 years of experience: $115,000 base salary
• More than 10 years of experience: $125,000 base salary

UVA Physicians Group Benefit Highlights

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
• Employer-sponsored retirement savings plans with employer contributions and pre-tax/Roth savings options.
• Generous paid time off, paid holidays, and leave benefits.
• Employer-paid life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage.
• CME/professional development support
• Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) eligibility for many positions.

The University of Virginia is an equal opportunity employer. All interested persons are encouraged to apply, including veterans and individuals with disabilities. Learn more about UVA’s commitment to non-discrimination and equal opportunity employment.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Job requires standing for prolonged periods, frequently bending/stooping, reaching (overhead, extensive, and repetitive); Repetitive motion: computer keyboard. Proficient communicative, auditory and visual skills; Attention to detail and ability to write legibly; Ability to lift/push/pull 50 - 100lbs. May be exposed to noise, radiation, radioactive materials, blood/body fluids and infectious disease.

Job Summary

Wentworth-Douglass Hospital is a community hospital located in Dover, New Hampshire, about 70 miles north of Boston and is a part of Mass General Brigham network. WDH Women & Children’s Center currently has over 1700 deliveries per year and offers complete family-focused care, making it the delivery destination for the New Hampshire Seacoast. The centerpiece of the WDH Newborn Program is a 12-bed Level IIB Special Care Nursery, offering care to infants born at 32 weeks of gestation and higher. WDH’s close medical and nursing collaboration with the Mass General Brigham Academic Medical Centers ensures the most advanced approach to infant care.

The qualified candidate will be joining a dynamic group of advanced practice practitioners and physicians, led by a neonatologist medical director. Newborn and Pediatric services at WDH are supported by MGH pediatric subspecialties, including pediatric cardiology, pulmonary, endocrinology and gastroenterology.

Delivery Room Services
The APP will provide delivery room (DR) coverage at WDH. DR coverage responsibilities include attending high risk deliveries upon request, providing neonatal resuscitation, evaluating newborns in the delivery room and newborn nurseries. The APP will provide all necessary in-house and outpatient prenatal neonatology consultations requested by obstetric staff. The APP will work collaboratively with a supervising physician who will generally not be on-site. In addition, the program will be supported with the 24/7 availability from neonatologists based in the MGH Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.

Newborn Nursery
The APP will manage infants in the Newborn Nursery as a primary provider in collaboration with supervising physician. This involves daily rounding, daily comprehensive assessments, review of patient data, and development of plans for all infants. Diagnoses are varied and include those infants who are experiencing delayed transition, mild respiratory distress, hypoglycemic infants, late preterm infants, convalescing preterm infants, and infants born to mothers with substance use disorder. Responsible for daily care, coordinating and planning discharge home, supporting and updating families, and conducting family meetings.

Level IIB NICU
The APP will manage infants in the Level IIB NICU as a primary provider. This involves daily rounding with a multidisciplinary team, daily comprehensive assessments, review of patient data, and development of plans for a caseload of infants. Diagnoses are varied and include those infants who are delivered at 32 weeks or greater, need CPAP or short-term ventilation, late preterm infants, convalescing preterm infants, and ESC infants. Responsible for daily care, coordinating and planning discharge home, supporting and updating families, conducting family meetings.

The Urgent Care Advanced Practice Provider (APP) provides direct and indirect care to patients and their families in an Urgent Care setting. This APP will function independently and collaboratively to provide medical care for patients from 0 through 20 years. This position will require the provider to work weekend days and weekday nights.

• Practices collaboratively with physicians and other health care providers to provide high quality health care to children.

• Performs ongoing assessment and evaluation of patient progress and revision of interdisciplinary plan of care.
• May use prescriptive authority if appropriately credentialed to do so. Collaborates interprofessionally as needed. Identifies patient/family need for further resources and initiates appropriate referrals.
• Documents of patient care and progress on patient's chart.
• Provides patient/family teaching based on identification of learning needs.

jobs.description:
Come join us - Nemours Children’s Hospital, Delaware is seeking an APRN/PA to join our Clinical Research team. This APRN/PA will function independently and collaboratively to provide specialty medical care for patients from 0 through 20 years participating in Clinical Research Trials. This position is Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 5:00pm with no nights or weekends.

The incumbent will coordinate, implement and complete clinical research studies or clinical trials by assisting with IRB submissions, assisting in regulatory document preparation and collection, in-servicing research teams, recruiting study participants, obtaining parental permission/assent, educating parents/participants, scheduling and conducting study procedures/examinations, collecting and recording study data, maintaining study records, interfacing with study sponsors, participation in sponsor study monitoring visits.

Excellent written, phone, and interpersonal communication skills are required. Interested applicants should possess the ability to function at a high level in an interprofessional team environment as well as an independent provider.

Essential Functions Include:

• Assessment, diagnosis, management, and follow up visits for patients enrolled in Clinical Research projects.
• Provide concise documentation of patient encounters including diagnoses, management strategies and follow up plan.
• Identifies patient and family needs for additional resources and initiates appropriate referrals.
• Provides patient and family teaching based on identified learning needs.
• Evaluates compliance with the prescribed treatment regimen through phone calls, emails, app messaging, patient/family assessments, and outpatient visits as needed.
• Acts as patient advocate and liaison.
• Acts as role model for other office members to foster professional development.
• Utilizes advanced knowledge and specialized skill in nursing practice in accordance with the state law, hospital bylaws, and hospital policy.
• Demonstrates proficiency in the care of all age groups Including neonates, Infants, toddlers, school-aged children, adolescents, and young adults.
• Responsible for participation in departmental initiatives and programmatic development including the identification of opportunities to improve services, offer recommendations, and implement actions as appropriate and consistent with the goals of the Nemours Foundation.

• Mentors new clinical research coordinators. Participates in training nursing and ancillary study staff for study purposes; recruits, screens and enrolls sufficient number of study participants in conformance with protocol requirements.

• Assists in the maintenance of study medication accountability records; prepares clinical specimens for shipment to central laboratories.

The Newborn/Infant Intensive Care Unit (N/IICU) at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia is a 100- bed Level IV unit with significant growth planned in the coming years. For more than 50 years, we've cared for critically ill babies with all types of conditions and congenital malformations using the latest technology and advances in neonatal medicine.

Our Nurse Practitioners and Physician Assistants provide care for neonates who need acute medical care, including multidisciplinary evaluations, complex surgical intervention, ECMO and special low-dose radiologic imaging.

The medical staff is organized into teams, led by a senior neonatologist. Fellows, neonatal nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and pediatric residents work with the neonatologists on each team to provide care for 12-18 babies. CHOP N/IICU APPs also have the opportunity to practice at our level III NICU at our King of Prussia and at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania.

jobs.title: Inpatient Nursery Nurse Practitioner, Part Time
jobs.summary: Inpatient Nursery Nurse Practitioner, Part Time at University of Maryland Upper Chesapeake Medical Center. Setting: mixed settings.
jobs.description:
Job Requirements

Some providers save lives. Some help bring them into the world.

If your ideal patient weighs less than 10 pounds, your best conversations are with new parents, and you believe every newborn deserves an exceptional start, we'd love to meet you.

University of Maryland Capital Region Health is seeking a compassionate and skilled Advanced Practice Provider to join our growing Nursery Team. This unique part-time opportunity allows you to care for newborns during one of the most important moments in their lives—while enjoying a flexible schedule and supportive team environment.

Why You'll Love This Role

Work with the cutest patient population in healthcare

Every day brings new beginnings as you care for healthy newborns and support families through those unforgettable first days.

Be part of a growing Women's & Children's program

Join a collaborative team committed to delivering exceptional newborn care within a rapidly expanding obstetrics service.

Part-Time Flexibility

This position is a 0.5 FTE equivalent, requiring just four 10-hour shifts every two weeks, making it ideal for providers seeking work-life balance while staying clinically engaged.

Grow Your Expertise

You'll receive training across all aspects of newborn nursery care, including inpatient coverage and home call responsibilities.

Please review 2026-2027 UMMS Benefits Guide.pdf

What You'll Do

As a valued member of our Nursery Team, you'll:

• Perform newborn assessments and daily rounds.
• Evaluate, diagnose, and manage newborn patients.
• Order and interpret diagnostic testing.
• Partner with physicians, nurses, and multidisciplinary team members to provide exceptional care.
• Educate and support new parents during a life-changing experience.
• Perform procedures including newborn circumcisions.
• Help families confidently transition from hospital to home.

The Ideal Candidate

You may be a great fit if you:

• Love working with newborns and their families.
• Enjoy patient education and building meaningful connections.
• Thrive in a collaborative, family-centered environment.
• Are organized, compassionate, and able to manage multiple priorities.
• Want to contribute to a culture focused on quality, safety, and exceptional patient experiences.

Qualifications

Nurse Practitioners

• Bachelor's degree in Nursing required.
• RN experience required.
• Completion of an Acute Care Nurse Practitioner program.
• Active Maryland NP license.

Physician Assistants

• Graduate of an ARC-PA accredited Physician Assistant program.
• NCCPA certification required.
• Active Maryland PA license.

Preferred Experience

• One year of nursery, newborn, pediatric, or related clinical experience.

Certifications

• BLS certification required.
• NRP certification preferred.
• Eligible for credentialing through the University of Maryland Capital Region Health Medical Staff Office.

Why UM Capital Region Health?

At UM Capital Region Health, our providers are more than clinicians—they are trusted partners, educators, advocates, and leaders. You'll join a team that values collaboration, professional development, patient safety, and compassionate care.

The Bottom Line

You'll help welcome new lives into the world.

You'll guide first-time parents through some of their most memorable moments.

And you'll go home knowing your work made a difference before a child even leaves the hospital.

All information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

We do not accept inquiries or solicitations from 3rd party recruiters/search firms.
